The Prophet was commanded to fight people until they testify there is no god but Allah, which protects their blood and property; Abu Bakr resolved to fight those withholding Zakat.
An enemy who says there is no god but Allah must not be killed, as Miqdad and Usama were told; whoever takes up arms against Muslims is not of them.
Inviting the enemy to Islam was needed early on, and Banu Mustaliq were raided unawares; commanders were to offer Islam, emigration or jizya before fighting, never mutilating or killing children.
War is a stratagem; do not wish to meet the enemy but ask Allah for safety, and when you meet them be firm: Paradise is under the shadows of swords.
Finding a woman killed in battle, the Prophet forbade killing women and children; asked about polytheists' women and children struck in night raids, he said they are from them.
Ibn Umar was turned away from fighting at Uhud aged fourteen and allowed at the Trench aged fifteen, which Umar b. Abd al-Aziz made the line between minor and adult.
Allah guarantees whoever fights in His way Paradise or return with reward and booty; his wound will smell of musk, and the Prophet longed to be killed again and again.
Jihad equals ceaseless fasting and prayer and ranks above serving pilgrims; a morning or evening of it outweighs the world, and it raises a man a hundred grades in Paradise.
The best man fights in Allah's way with life and wealth; next is one living apart in a mountain valley, worshipping his Lord and sparing people his harm.
Waking from a nap laughing, the Prophet said he was shown followers sailing the sea to fight like kings on thrones, and told Umm Haram she was among the first.
After Muslims killed a man who greeted them with peace and took his sheep, the verse came: do not tell one who greets you that he is not a Muslim.
